title: Case study: TF activity in memory vs. naive T cells
text: CD4+ T cells reshape regulatory programs differentiate naive memory state. case study uses methylTFR deviation scores ask focused question: transcription factors show differential activity memory naive T cells? reuse deviation matrices bundled package (tc_mem, tc_naive), analysis runs end--end without downloading hg38 annotation. See Get started vignette deviations computed raw WGBS data.

title: Case study: TF activity in memory vs. naive T cells
text: differential_deviation_test() compares deviation scores two groups per motif. two groups parametric = TRUE t-test, followed Benjamini-Hochberg correction. mean_difference column absolute difference mean deviation memory naive cells: larger values flag TFs whose binding-site methylation shifts differentiation.
code: tc_result <- differential_deviation_test(     deviations = devs,     groups = groups,     alternative = "two.sided",     parametric = TRUE,     padjMethod = "BH" )  tc_result <- tc_result[order(tc_result$p_value_adjusted), ] tc_result #>                  motifs      p_value p_value_adjusted mean_difference #> MAX::MYC       MAX::MYC 1.078111e-05     0.0001078111     0.093414294 #> IRF2               IRF2 1.873667e-03     0.0093683362     0.034142762 #> PPARG             PPARG 3.996324e-03     0.0133210805     0.034286836 #> FOXF2             FOXF2 1.694736e-02     0.0355317162     0.029207590 #> MZF1(var.2) MZF1(var.2) 1.776586e-02     0.0355317162     0.018508308 #> PAX6               PAX6 7.709712e-02     0.1284951966     0.021013722 #> RORA               RORA 2.084783e-01     0.2978261195     0.017159124 #> FOXD1             FOXD1 3.644010e-01     0.4555013119     0.010816363 #> RORA(var.2) RORA(var.2) 5.172906e-01     0.5747672942     0.007677473 #> PBX1               PBX1 6.785692e-01     0.6785692148     0.003544582

title: Case study: TF activity in memory vs. naive T cells
text: visualise motifs effect size, highlighting passing FDR cutoff 0.05.
code: tc_result$motifs <- factor(     tc_result$motifs,     levels = tc_result$motifs[order(tc_result$mean_difference)] ) tc_result$significant <- ifelse(     tc_result$p_value_adjusted < 0.05,     "FDR < 0.05", "n.s." )  ggplot(tc_result, aes(x = mean_difference, y = motifs, colour = significant)) +     ggplot2::geom_segment(         aes(x = 0, xend = mean_difference, yend = motifs),         colour = "grey70"     ) +     ggplot2::geom_point(size = 3) +     ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(         values = c("FDR < 0.05" = "#E66100", "n.s." = "grey50")     ) +     ggplot2::labs(         x = "Mean deviation difference (memory vs. naive)",         y = NULL, colour = NULL,         title = "Differential TF activity"     ) +     theme_classic() +     theme(legend.position = "bottom")

title: Case study: TF activity in memory vs. naive T cells
text: TFs top ranking strongest candidates driving memory-specific regulatory changes: binding sites lose gain methylation cells transition naive state. hits natural starting point footprint inspection (plotExpectedFootprint(), shown main vignette) follow-larger cohort. bundled data small subset (10 motifs, 5 samples per group), values illustrative. full BLUEPRINT memory T-cell panel workflow scales thousands motifs via run_methyltfr().

title: methylTFR: Quantification of DNA Methylation Signatures in Transcription Factor Binding Sites
text: DNA methylation can modulate transcription factor (TF) binding, particularly occurring within transcription factor binding sites (TFBS). methylTFR R package identifies DNA methylation signatures TFBS using whole-genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS) data. sample, methylation levels first aggregated across genomic regions corresponding TFBS. yields observed deviation, captures raw signal methylation enrichment depletion TF. account sequence composition biases, methylTFR estimates expected deviation using genomic background models derived TF motif GC content genome-wide GC frequency. deviation matrix provides compact interpretable representation TFBS methylation across samples, suitable downstream analyses dimensionality reduction (e.g., PCA, UMAP), clustering, differential testing, visualization TF-specific methylation footprints.

title: methylTFR: Quantification of DNA Methylation Signatures in Transcription Factor Binding Sites
text: can install stable release methylTFR Bioconductor using: install development version directly GitHub:
code: if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {   install.packages("BiocManager") }  BiocManager::install("methylTFR") if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE)) {   install.packages("remotes") } remotes::install_github("EpigenomeInformatics/methylTFR")

title: methylTFR: Quantification of DNA Methylation Signatures in Transcription Factor Binding Sites
text: read_methylome() function used import single-sample DNA methylation data GRanges object. supports several common file formats, including EPP, ALLC, BisSNP, bismarkCytosine, bismarkcov, ENCODE. can optionally filter low-coverage sites using cov_threshold parameter (default = 1), excludes positions insufficient read support. example reading example EPP-formatted file provided package:

title: methylTFR: Quantification of DNA Methylation Signatures in Transcription Factor Binding Sites
text: provide precomputed TFBS-based annotation data human genome (hg38), required methylTFR compute expected deviations. includes transcription factor binding sites, GC content windows, motif GC frequency models. can download hg38-compatible annotation package following AWS-hosted archive: Download methylTFRAnnotationsHg38.tar.gz Optionally, can create customized annotation package use methylTFR using methylTFRAnnotationBuilder package available GitHub.

title: methylTFR: Quantification of DNA Methylation Signatures in Transcription Factor Binding Sites
text: methylTFR relies several precomputed annotation resources estimate expected methylation levels transcription factor binding sites (TFBS). annotations include: GC distribution (gcdist_subset): Genome-wide GC content distribution around cytosines, used model methylation expectations. Motif GC frequency (BATF_gcfreqs): GC frequency profile specific BATF motif across TFBS, used correct sequence composition bias. TF binding sites (BATF_tf_bindsites): GRanges object containing genomic coordinates BATF binding sites. Example methylation data (example_data): small subset methylation calls EPP format, read using read_methylome() function, provided demonstration purposes. following code loads example datasets displays first entries:

what: Compute Deviation Score for a Single Sample and Single Motif
title: methylTFR: Quantification of DNA Methylation Signatures in Transcription Factor Binding Sites
text: computeDeviation() function calculates deviation score specific transcription factor (TF) motif single sample. compares observed methylation TF binding sites (TFBS) expected methylation derived GC frequency models. example uses BATF motif example methylation dataset loaded earlier. methylation data must first binned GC content using addGCBintoMethylome() computing deviation.
code: # Add GC bins to methylation data bin_meth <- addGCBintoMethylome(msites, gcdist, ignoreStrand = TRUE) bin_meth #>      gcbin avg_mscore #> [1,]     1  0.5315789 #> [2,]     2  0.6466688 #> [3,]     3  0.7217031 #> [4,]     4  0.7091566 #> [5,]     5  0.7838198  # Compute deviation score for BATF motif deviation_score <- computeDeviation(     motif = "BATF",     msites = msites,     tf_bindsites = tf_bindsites,     gcfreqs = gcfreqs,     enhancer = NULL,     ignoreStrand = TRUE,     binMsites = bin_meth )  # View the result deviation_score #>         dev   exp_dev #>       <num>     <num> #> 1: 1.743674 0.9835985

what: Run methylTFR on multiple samples and motifs
title: methylTFR: Quantification of DNA Methylation Signatures in Transcription Factor Binding Sites
text: methylTFR package provides run_methyltfr function run analysis multiple samples motif sites. need download annotation package human genome (hg38) place working directory.
code: library(methylTFRAnnotationHg38) # annotation package for hg38  gcfreqs <- getGCfreq(motifSet = "jaspar2020") gc_dist <- getGenomeGC("hg38") tf_bindsites <- getTFbindsites(motifSet = "jaspar2020")  sample_dir <- file.path("samples_dir") sample_ann <- "samples.tsv" # should contain column name bedFile  # deviation score matrix deviations <- run_methyltfr(sample_ann, # sample annotation file     sample_dir, # where the EPP files are     threads = 8, # number of threads     chunkSize = 10, # number of chunks to process     sampleColName = "bedFile", # column name for EPP file paths in sample_ann     tf_bindsites = tf_bindsites, # TF binding sites     gcfreqs = gcfreqs, # GC frequency     gc_dist = gc_dist, # GC distribution     filetype = "EPP" # file type )

title: methylTFR: Quantification of DNA Methylation Signatures in Transcription Factor Binding Sites
text: visually assess observed methylation patterns compare expected profiles transcription factor binding sites (TFBS), methylTFR provides plotExpectedFootprint() function. generates footprint plot given motif single sample, allowing inspect local methylation behavior relative GC-derived expectations. example , visualize methylation footprint BATF motif using included example data.
code: # Generate footprint plot for BATF p <- plotExpectedFootprint(     motif = "BATF",     tf_bindsites = tf_bindsites,     msites = msites_sub,     sample_name = "ExampleSample",     gc_dist = gcdist,     gcfreqs = gcfreqs,     enhancer = NULL,     returnPlotData = FALSE )  p

title: methylTFR: Quantification of DNA Methylation Signatures in Transcription Factor Binding Sites
text: assess differential TF activity two groups samples, methylTFR provides differential_deviation_test() function. function computes observed expected deviation scores TF motif across specified groups, enabling statistical testing identify differentially active TFs. methylTFRdeviations object looked like:
code: load(system.file("extdata", "tc_mem.rda", package = "methylTFR")) load(system.file("extdata", "tc_naive.rda", package = "methylTFR")) devs <- cbind(tc_mem, tc_naive) devs #> class: methylTFRdeviations  #> dim: 10 10  #> metadata(0): #> assays(2): deviations z #> rownames(10): FOXF2 FOXD1 ... RORA RORA(var.2) #> rowData names(1): motifs #> colnames(10): Tc-Mem_OP_S5_Long_D1.bedGraph.bed #>   Tc-Mem_OP_S4_Long_D60.bedGraph.bed ... #>   Tc-Naive_OP_S4_Long_D1.bedGraph.bed #>   Tc-Naive_OP_S3_High_D1.bedGraph.bed #> colData names(4): CommonMinID condition cell_type bedFile # Construct group labels from sample names get_groupname <- function(x) {     return(unlist(strsplit(x, split = "_"))[1]) } groups <- sub(     ".bedGraph", "",     unlist(lapply(         FUN = get_groupname,         X = colnames(devs)     )) ) table(groups) #> groups #>   Tc-Mem Tc-Naive  #>        5        5  # Run the differential deviation test tc_result <- differential_deviation_test(     deviations = devs,     groups = groups,     alternative = "two.sided",     parametric = TRUE,     padjMethod = "BH" )  # View the results head(tc_result) #>                  motifs      p_value p_value_adjusted mean_difference #> FOXF2             FOXF2 1.694736e-02     0.0355317162      0.02920759 #> FOXD1             FOXD1 3.644010e-01     0.4555013119      0.01081636 #> IRF2               IRF2 1.873667e-03     0.0093683362      0.03414276 #> MZF1(var.2) MZF1(var.2) 1.776586e-02     0.0355317162      0.01850831 #> MAX::MYC       MAX::MYC 1.078111e-05     0.0001078111      0.09341429 #> PPARG             PPARG 3.996324e-03     0.0133210805      0.03428684
